title: moorland-microloan-onramp-scratchnote
summary: Working notes from discovery/onramp calls with Moorland Microloan. High-level requirements for KYC, credit-assist conversational flows, fraud embeddings, and deployment constraints (EU data residency + VPC).
body:
Context:
- Customer: Moorland Microloan (small fintech lending platform, EU-first footprint).
- Use cases discussed: automated KYC assistant for onboarding, short-form credit decision assistant (structured Q->score), and semantic search over customer docs for fraud flags.
- Primary ask: POC within 6 weeks to validate latency and quality, then Private / VPC deployment if ops/legal satisfied.

Call notes (2026-02-22, 45m):
- Attendees: Moorland CTO Anil Kapoor, Head of Ops Priya Shah, Product Tomasz Nowak; Redwood: Maya (CS), Jordan (Eng), Samir (Perf).
- Business constraints: EU data residency mandatory; no PHI but heavy PII (IDs, addresses). Retention policy: 7 years for audit, but they prefer not to store raw PII in logs.
- Latency SLO: 90th percentile <= 150ms for single-turn KYC prompts (concerned for UX on mobile). Throughput: ~25 qps peak per region, steady 5–8 qps.
- Cost target: keep hosted inference cost under €0.003/token equivalent at scale; willing to accept dedicated pricing for predictable commit.
- Model quality: prefer open models with deterministic behavior for regulatory traceability. Interested in 7B quantized variants (we suggested an open-llama-style 7B 4bit baseline).
- Observability: need per-request trace (no raw PII persisted), redaction in logs, and auditability for every rollout.

Technical requirements (explicit):
- Deployment: Private control plane + VPC peering into Moorland AWS eu-west-1. Option to run on-prem later but start with VPC.
- Network: allowlist Redwood egress IPs, need TLS mutual auth for control plane.
- Keys: integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS) for key management.
- Data flow: PII touches user device -> Moorland backend -> Redwood inference over VPC -> model output. Moorland wants optional client-side PII tokenization step before sending.
- Logging: redacted payloads stored in audit logs; full-text only retained in encrypted blob accessible to compliance team on-demand (separate backup bucket in EU).
- Models & fallbacks: primary model = quantized 7B tuned for instruction/chat; fallback small 3B distilled model for burst traffic with automatic routing policy.
- Batching/caching: want intelligent batching for embeddings and caching for repeated prefix prompts for onboarding flows.

Gotchas / risks called out in meeting:
- PII in prompt: Moorland unwilling to send raw ID numbers into third-party logs. We need to ensure prefix/KV cache does not leak tokens into telemetry.
- Latency vs batching: their 150ms SLO makes batching dangerous for KYC unless we use continuous batching with strict cap. Need to test tail-latency on target hardware.
- Quantized model quality: 4-bit quantization may degrade certain scoring heuristics – must include evals on their prompt corpus.
- Legal: retention 7 years may conflict with our default log retention; confirm archival steps and access controls.
- Network ops: VPC peering and mutual TLS will add setup time (estimated 2–3 weeks by infra).

Suggested approach (quick POC path):
1) Short lab bench (1 week): run local perf tests: quantized 7B vs 3B distilled on Dedicated hardware profile (A100-like). Measure p95/p99 latency for 16–64 token responses and throughput at 1–25 qps. Owner: Samir. (Jira INF-982)
2) Privacy gating (1 week): implement prompt-side redaction helper + sample transform script for Moorland to run client-side. Owner: Jordan. (Jira CS-437)
3) Integration POC (2–3 weeks): Private deployment MVP in eu-west-1 with VPC peering, minimal RBAC + KMS integration, canary to 10% traffic using rollouts. Owner: Maya + Eng on call.
4) Eval + quality sign-off (1 week): run their test prompts (we requested 500 sample prompts, they agreed to share 150 anonymized examples first).

Immediate open questions (need answers from customer):
- Which specific fields are considered PII vs "business-identifiers" for them? (Priya to provide list)
- Is there an in-house tokenization/redaction service they prefer us to integrate with, or will they run our transform script?
- Backup/archive access: who in Moorland gets access to the encrypted audit blobs? Legal contact?
- SLA expectations post-POC: do they require financial SLA or operational (uptime + response time) only?

Action items (short):
- Maya: send architecture sketch + sample VPC peering checklist (due 2026-03-05).
- Jordan: deliver prompt-redaction Python snippet + Dockerized transformer for client (due 2026-03-10).
- Samir: perf bench report (quantized 7B vs 3B) with p50/p95/p99 and token/sec numbers (due 2026-03-08).
- Elena (legal): reach out to Moorland legal (Priya/Anil) to confirm retention/access and sign DPA addendum (due 2026-03-12).

Misc notes / heuristics from convo:
- They like stable deterministic outputs for audit; recommend pinning model version and disabling ONNX-style runtime non-deterministic kernels for canary runs.
- Suggested fallback policy: route to smaller model + synthetic explanation when primary is overloaded, rather than queueing. (They prefer fail-fast UX).
- Potential future: embeddings-indexed transaction history for fraud signals; storage must be encrypted and labelled PII.

Reference links shared in call:
- Moorland internal risk policy (they will drop link to confluence after legal review).
- Redwood rollout docs (sent by Maya during call)

Notes to self:
- Need to draft an internal ticket that combines network ops + privacy + perf bench. Link to infra PR for private control plane (GH PR #342).
- Keep PII examples as synthetic in evals.

Next meeting: schedule technical deep-dive (network + KMS + redaction) week of 2026-03-15. Aim to have perf bench and redaction script before that meeting.

Quick capture of sample prompt they shared: 
- "Given applicant profile (income, months-on-job, past defaults summary) return a short credit_score_label and 3 bullet rationales (do not include SSN or ID numbers)."

Tone/behavior note: CTO wants conservative defaults (auditability > aggressive cost optimizations). Keep that in proposal.

---- end of scratchnote ----

Elena: confirm legal on data residency/backups (DPA addendum) by 2026-03-12
